# Work Tracker

The tracker is an append-only event log. Ledger mode writes `.basicly/ledger/`, committed with the code. With `.basicly-tracker.toml`, writes queue vault events beside the clone; own pending writes are visible and marked `pending` until shared.
The kit is `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py`, which needs nothing installed. The engine is `basicly tracker`, which works when `basicly` is on PATH.

## Steps

```sh
python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py ready .basicly/ledger
python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py create .basicly/ledger --title "Fix the flaky clock test" \
  --field issue_type=task --field size=small \
  --description "## Context
When the suite runs in parallel, the clock test fails." \
  --acceptance "When the suite runs with -n 8, the clock test shall pass."
python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py claim .basicly/ledger RECORD-ID
python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py confirm .basicly/ledger RECORD-ID --evidence JSON
python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py close .basicly/ledger RECORD-ID --reason "why"
```

1. **Find or file the record before the work.** Give it a `## Context` and at least one acceptance criterion; a record bigger than `size=small` also needs `review --evidence` before the claim. Run `create` alone and read the id from its reply; the `tracker-commit-msg` hook refuses a commit that names an id the ledger does not hold.
2. **Claim it before the first edit.** In ledger mode, push so others can see it. In vault mode, use the native canonical claim, then set `in_progress` through update; the claim has its own exit codes and does not bypass readiness. A refusal names its remedy; follow it before retrying.
3. **Confirm, then close it** once the whole task is done: `confirm` records each criterion with its command and result, as `{"checks": [{"criterion": "...", "command": ["argv"], "result": "what you saw", "exit_code": 0}]}`, and `close` refuses without it.
4. **Commit with the id in the subject.** In ledger mode, stage the code and `.basicly/ledger` together; make no separate close commit. Vault mode writes no local ledger events.

When `basicly` is on PATH, `basicly tracker write -- ...` runs the writes through the engine with the grammar in [write](references/write.md). An engine claim is `update RECORD-ID --status in_progress` in ledger mode; vault mode needs the native canonical claim first. The write reference classifies all 15 vault forms and their remedies.

## Rules

- **Never take a record that someone holds.** `ready` names each holder; `--take` is for an agreed handover only. Ledger mode uses `--to`, else `BASICLY_HOLDER`, else `git config basicly.holder`, else your git name. Vault claims use your chosen `BASICLY_HOLDER` or `basicly.holder`, else writer/session ids. Choose a pseudonym before publishing a name.
- **Name a record by its title, with the id as the address.** A person cannot read a bare id.
- **Never edit, delete or reorder a line in an event file.** Append the write that supersedes the wrong one.
- **Probe against a scratch ledger directory, never the live one:** `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py create "$(mktemp -d)" --prefix probe --title probe`. The log has no undo.
- **Check the output shape before you parse it.** `show` on an absent record prints `{"found": false}`. The kit `create` prints JSON; read its `record` field. The engine `create` prints `created: RECORD-ID`, or JSON with `--json`.
- **Use one ledger per repository, never one per worktree.** The git-ignored `.basicly/ledger/redirect` points every worktree at the same log.

## Read when needed

- For selective reads, history or the served page, read [read](references/read.md).
- Before a write, review or close, read [write](references/write.md) for the grammar and the Context, Acceptance and evidence contracts.
- For imports, shard folding or bulk queries, read [maintenance](references/maintenance.md).
